Super Eagles striker Tolu Arokodare has revealed how visa difficulties nearly ended his ambition of pursuing a professional football career in Europe. The Nigerian forward disclosed that he missed several opportunities with European clubs despite attracting interest, including French side Toulouse and Belgian outfit Royal Charleroi. Speaking on the Counter Attack Podcast, Arokodare recounted how repeated visa setbacks threatened his attempts to establish himself abroad. “I almost lost the opportunity to play football because of my green card. Toulouse wanted me, but I was denied a visa. Victor Osimhen helped me get an offer from Charleroi, but I was denied again. Valmiera wanted me, but there was no Latvian embassy in Nigeria,” he said. The striker also revealed that Osimhen, who was playing for Charleroi at the time, personally contacted the club’s president to help facilitate the move. However, the proposed transfer fell through because of the visa complications. Arokodare eventually secured an opportunity with Latvian club Valmiera in 2019, although the move also presented logistical challenges because Latvia did not have an embassy in Nigeria at the time. He subsequently developed his career through spells in Germany, France and Belgium before earning a move to the Premier League with Wolverhampton Wanderers. Despite the setbacks, the forward persevered and eventually established himself in European football, with Osimhen’s intervention representing one of the opportunities that could have accelerated his breakthrough.
